NEW SECTION . 263C.1 Definitions. 6 As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise 7 requires: 8 1. “Board” means the state board of regents. 9 2. “Center” means the center for intellectual freedom 10 established by section 263C.2. 11 3. “Regents institution” means an institution specified in 12 section 262.7, subsections 1 through 3. 13 4. “University” means the state university of Iowa. 14 Sec. 3. NEW SECTION . 263C.2 Center for intellectual 15 freedom. 16 1. A center for intellectual freedom is established as an 17 independent academic center under the board at the university. 18 2. The center shall conduct teaching and research in the 19 historical ideas, traditions, and texts that have shaped the 20 American constitutional order and society. 21 3. The board may name the center in accordance with any 22 philanthropic naming policies or practices of the board or 23 university. 24 Sec. 4. NEW SECTION . 263C.3 Functions of the center. 25 1. The center shall provide scholarship in all of the 26 following subjects: 27 a. The texts and major debates that form the intellectual 28 foundation of free societies, especially that of the United 29 States. 30 b. The principles, ideals, and institutions of the American 31 constitutional order. 32 c. The foundations of responsible leadership and informed 33 citizenship. 34 2. The center shall offer university-wide programming 35 -1- SF 519.1462 (2) 91 (amending this SF 519 to CONFORM to HF 437) je/jh 1/ 5 #1. related to the values of free speech and civil discourse. 1 3. The center shall work to do all of the following: 2 a. Expand the intellectual diversity of the university’s 3 academic community. 4 b. Foster civic engagement among university students and 5 faculty. 6 c. Coordinate with the center for cyclone civics at Iowa 7 state university and the center for civic education at the 8 university of northern Iowa to enable academic offerings that 9 may be offered to students at any of the regents institutions 10 either in person or online. 11 4. The center, in collaboration with any of the regents 12 institutions, may offer courses; develop certificate, minor, 13 and major programs as well as graduate programs; and offer 14 degrees. 15 5. The center shall offer at least one three-semester 16 credit hour course in American history and civil government. 17 If a regents institution has established general education 18 requirements for undergraduate students that include an 19 American heritage course requirement, the center shall ensure 20 that the course satisfies that requirement. The center shall 21 coordinate with the center for cyclone civics at Iowa state 22 university and the center for civic education at the university 23 of northern Iowa to ensure that the course is offered to 24 students at each regents institution either in person or 25 online. 26 Sec. 5. NEW SECTION . 263C.4 Bylaws. 27 The center shall establish bylaws governing the center 28 subject to the approval of the board. In addition to any 29 other bylaws established, the bylaws must include all of the 30 following requirements, which shall take precedence over any 31 other requirements in the bylaws: 32 1. The center shall educate students by means of free, open, 33 and rigorous intellectual inquiry to seek the truth. 34 2. The center affirms its duty to equip students with 35 -2- SF 519.1462 (2) 91 (amending this SF 519 to CONFORM to HF 437) je/jh 2/ 5 the skills, habits, and dispositions of mind they need to 1 reach their own informed conclusions on matters of social and 2 political importance. 3 3. The center affirms the value of intellectual diversity 4 in higher education and aspires to enhance the intellectual 5 diversity of the university. 6 4. The center affirms a commitment to create a community 7 dedicated to an ethic of civil and free inquiry, which respects 8 the intellectual freedom of each member, supports individual 9 capacities for growth, and welcomes the differences of opinion 10 that naturally exist in a public university community. 11 Sec. 6. NEW SECTION . 263C.5 Funding —— use. 12 1. The center may accept and administer private and 13 external donations and gifts. The university of Iowa center 14 for advancement shall be the designated foundation for 15 philanthropic gifts or funding for the center. 16 2. Any moneys appropriated to the center, and any private 17 and external donations to the center, shall be used only for 18 the direct operation of the center. 19 3. Any additional funding required to operate the center 20 shall be proportionally provided by the regents institutions, 21 subject to approval of the board. 22 Sec. 7. NEW SECTION . 263C.6 Center faculty. 23 The university shall employ tenure-eligible faculty members 24 to provide instruction through the center. The university 25 shall incrementally increase the number of such faculty to five 26 based on market research and student demand. Faculty members 27 appointed to the center may hold joint appointments to other 28 academic units of the university. Faculty members who are not 29 affiliated with the center shall have no authority to approve, 30 deny, or modify the terms of appointment of faculty to the 31 center. 32 Sec. 8. NEW SECTION . 263C.7 Advisory council. 33 1. No later than December 31, 2025, the board shall appoint 34 an advisory council for the center. 35 -3- SF 519.1462 (2) 91 (amending this SF 519 to CONFORM to HF 437) je/jh 3/ 5 2. The board shall appoint a minimum of nine members to the 1 council. A majority of the members appointed to the council 2 shall constitute a quorum. No more than one member of the 3 council may be an employee of the university. 4 3. The board shall determine the initial length of each 5 member’s term in accordance with this subsection. A majority 6 of the members initially appointed to the council shall serve 7 initial terms of four years. The remaining initially appointed 8 members shall serve initial terms of two years. The board 9 shall appoint new members to fill vacancies on the council in 10 accordance with this section. 11 Sec. 9. NEW SECTION . 263C.8 Appointment of director. 12 1. The advisory council established under section 263C.7 13 shall conduct a nationwide search for candidates for the 14 director of the center. The council shall adhere to all 15 relevant state and federal laws in conducting the search. The 16 council shall submit finalists for the position to the board. 17 The board, upon approval of a candidate, shall appoint the 18 candidate as the director. All subsequent directors shall be 19 chosen in the same manner. 20 2. The director shall have the academic standing to be 21 eligible for tenure at a regents institution. 22 Sec. 10. NEW SECTION . 263C.9 Duties of director. 23 1. The director of the center shall have the sole and 24 exclusive authority to manage the recruitment and hiring 25 process, and to extend offers for employment, of the center 26 and to terminate employment of all staff of the center in 27 accordance with state and federal law. 28 2. The director shall conduct a market assessment to 29 determine course demand and the number of faculty required to 30 meet any unmet needs of the center and may conduct additional 31 market assessments as needed. A market assessment shall 32 include the subjects described in section 263C.3, subsections 1 33 and 2. 34 3.
